land.text: Mari and the middle Euphrates, 'destroyed and burned by' Sargon c. 2290

successors.note: Mari was 'deserted for two generations' before Manishtushu restored it under a Shakkanakku (Ididish, c. 2266); the Shakkanakku state (independent under Shar-kali-sharri, under Ur's hegemony later) and the Lim dynasty (c. 1830–1761) need their own dossiers.

capitals.name: Mari (Tell Hariri)
capitals.note: 11 km northwest of Abu Kamal, Deir ez-Zor Governorate, 'on the Euphrates' western bank'; abandoned c. 2550–2500 between the first and second cities.

correction.text: the first city of Mari, 'Built c. 2900 BC', founded 'at the time of ED I' (Early Dynastic page), abandoned c. 2550

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Mari. The radius is this dossier's; the page gives no border for the first kingdom.

correction.text: the second kingdom's middle Euphrates, from Terqa downstream toward Hit; Mari 'fought many wars against Ebla during the 24th century BC' and Iblul-Il 'invaded Eblaite cities on the middle Euphrates' upstream

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the second kingdom ('rebuilt before 2500 BC'). The river strip is this dossier's reading: the page names Terqa and the Euphrates cities but no border; the upstream cities (Emar) are Ebla's and are left to the ebla dossier.

ledger.note: 2900 BCE: Mari is built. Infobox 'Built c. 2900 BC'; the Early Dynastic page: 'Mari was founded at the time of ED I'.
2550 BCE: the first city is abandoned. 'The first city was abandoned c. 2550 BC, at the end of Early Dynastic II'. The state has no land until the second city.

region.text: the second city and its middle Euphrates

ledger.note: 2500 BCE: the second kingdom. 'The city was rebuilt before 2500 BC'. The river strip is this dossier's reading.

region.text: the Eblaite cities on the middle Euphrates

ledger.note: 2450 BCE: the war with Ebla. 'Kun-Damu of Ebla defeated Mari in the middle of the 25th century BC'; Sa'umu of Mari had 'conquered many Eblaite cities' (Ebla page). Eannatum of Lagash 'demanded tribute as far as Mari' in the same years (recorded in lagash as vassal_start -2450).

region.text: Ebla, which 'paid tribute to Mari under Igrish-Halam'

ledger.note: 2360 BCE: Ebla pays tribute to Mari. 'Ebla later paid tribute to Mari under Igrish-Halam, and the Mariote king Iblul-Il invaded Eblaite cities on the middle Euphrates'; undated, before Irkab-Damu's recovery c. 2340. Year bridged.
2340 BCE: 'Ebla recovered under Irkab-Damu in about 2340 BC and counter-attacked Mari'.

2300 BCE: the Ebla war ends. 'Ebla's first destruction came in c. 2300 BC, after Mari's war with Ebla, which included a Mariote victory at Terqa' (the Ebla page gives the Terqa victory to Ebla's vizier Ibbi-Sipish and has Mari destroy Ebla 'in revenge for Terqa' for Archi and Biga).

2290 BCE: Sargon destroys Mari. 'Just a decade after Ebla's destruction (c. 2300 BC middle chronology), Mari itself was destroyed and burned by' Sargon of Akkad; Astour dates it c. 2265 on the short chronology. 'Mari was deserted for two generations' before Manishtushu restored it under a Shakkanakku.

wars.name: Ebla–Mari war

zones.text: the Eblaite cities on the middle Euphrates

wars.outcome: Sa'umu took Eblaite cities; Kun-Damu defeated Mari (mid-25th century); Ebla paid tribute under Igrish-Halam and Iblul-Il invaded the middle Euphrates; Irkab-Damu recovered c. 2340; a battle at Terqa (claimed by both pages for different sides); Ebla burned c. 2300.

wars.name: Sargon's destruction of Mari
wars.outcome: Mari 'destroyed and burned' by Sargon a decade after Ebla; deserted for two generations.

certainty.note: A river kingdom known from its capital and the towns it fought over; no page gives a border, and the strip along the Euphrates is this dossier's reading.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks: Mari's first and second kingdoms in one dossier, -2900..-2290, with the fifty-year abandonment (c. 2550–2500) recorded as a loss to and gain from nobody; the reviewer may prefer two dossiers (first kingdom -2900..-2550, second -2500..-2290). The infobox gives no separate dates for the kingdoms; the text's dates are used. Mari's later lives are other states: the Shakkanakku dynasty (Ididish appointed c. 2266 under Manishtushu, independent as Akkad 'disintegrated under Shar-Kali-Sharri', 'nominally under Ur hegemony', ended 'not long before' the Lim dynasty) and the Amorite Lim dynasty (Yaggid-Lim c. 1830, Yahdun-Lim c. 1820–1798, Shamshi-Adad's annexation, Zimri-Lim c. 1776–1761, Hammurabi's destruction c. 1761 and razing c. 1759). Both are for me-02 or a gap-filler. The tribute to Lagash c. 2450 is recorded from Lagash's side. Mari resolves in the gazetteer; Terqa, Tuttul, Hit, Emar do not.
